title: Describe density
intro: Percent density compares measured in-place density with a defined reference density. The reference is part of the result. Saying only “the density is 94%” leaves out information needed to interpret it.

sections.title: Define Section 502
sections.text:
Section 502.11 of the supplied 2006 document uses different references for Marshall and Superpave mixtures. The Marshall expression divides in-place density by the density of the plant briquette. The Superpave expression divides in-place density by maximum theoretical density determined by the specified procedure. Use compatible units, the applicable method and representative results from the correct lot.

A core and a nuclear gauge do not produce evidence through the same procedure. Follow the approved sampling, testing, calibration/correlation and reporting requirements. Nuclear gauge operation requires the applicable CNSC licensing, training and controls; reading this chapter does not authorize it. Record location, lift, sample/gauge identification, method, density units and reference result. Avoid substituting a different day’s reference because it produces a more favourable percentage.

The dated tables E-1 and E-2 use different acceptance/payment bands. For example, a Marshall lot average of 97.6–98.0% has a +$0.50/t adjustment, while the Superpave +$0.50/t band is 93.0–93.9%. These bands cannot be exchanged. Sub-lot limits, rejection provisions and the other acceptance requirements also apply. A satisfactory lot mean can conceal an unacceptable individual area.

Compaction effort, temperature, mixture behaviour, support and rolling pattern affect the outcome. More passes are not automatically better: they may be ineffective after cooling or damage an unstable mat. Use the approved pattern and quality feedback to guide authorized changes.

worked.title: Two legitimate references, two different percentages
worked.case: In-place density is 2.340 Mg/m³. A fictional plant briquette result is 2.400 Mg/m³; maximum theoretical density is 2.500 Mg/m³.
worked.solution: Marshall-style comparison: 2.340/2.400 × 100 = 97.50%. Maximum-theoretical comparison: 2.340/2.500 × 100 = 93.60%. Both calculations are arithmetic examples; use only the reference required for the actual mixture and contract.

activities.prompt: For 2.325 Mg/m³ in place and 2.500 Mg/m³ maximum theoretical, calculate percent.
activities.answer: 2.325/2.500 × 100 = 93.00%. Identify the reference as maximum theoretical density and retain the actual method and lot details.
activities.title: For 2.325 Mg/m³ in place and 2.500 Mg/m³ maximum theoretical, calculate percent.

activities.prompt: A 400 t fictional Superpave lot average is 93.4%. Find the isolated dated table adjustment, then name two checks still needed.
activities.answer: 400 × $0.50 = +$200. Still check sub-lot/rejection requirements and all other acceptance parameters; verify the correct edition, reference and valid test results.
activities.title: A 400 t fictional Superpave lot average is 93.4%

activities.prompt: A spreadsheet divides every test by a fixed 2.400. What should a reviewer do?
activities.answer: Check mixture, lot and required reference; replace the unsupported constant with a traceable approved reference for each applicable calculation. Preserve the original record and document the correction.
